'''Hilda Lucia Solis''' ({{IPAc-en|s|oʊ|ˈ|l|iː|s}};{{refn|{{MerriamWebsterDictionary|Solis}}}} born October 20, 1957) is an American politician and member-elect of the [[United States House of Representatives]] for the [[California's 38th congressional district|38th congressional district]] of [[California]]. Solis is the outgoing  member of the [[Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors]] for the 1st district and is the [[Chair of Los Angeles County]]. Solis previously served as the 25th [[United States Secretary of Labor]] from 2009 to 2013, as part of the [[Obama administration|administration]] of [[President of the United States|President]] [[Barack Obama]]. She is a member of the [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic Party]] and previously served in the House of Representatives from 2001 to 2009, representing the [[California's 31st congressional district|31st]] and [[California's 32nd congressional district|32nd congressional districts]] of [[California]] that include [[East Los Angeles, California|East Los Angeles]] and the [[San Gabriel Valley]].

Solis was raised in [[La Puente, California]], by immigrant farmers from [[Nicaragua]] and [[Mexico]]. She earned degrees from the [[California State Polytechnic University, Pomona]] and the [[University of Southern California]] and worked for two federal agencies in [[Washington, D.C.]] Returning to her native state, she was elected to the [[Rio Hondo College|Rio Hondo Community College]] Board of Trustees in 1985, the [[California State Assembly]] in 1992, and the [[California State Senate]] in 1994. She was the first [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Hispanic]] woman to serve in the State Senate, and was reelected there in 1998. Solis sought to pass [[environmental justice]] legislation. She was the first female recipient of the [[Profile in Courage Award|John F. Kennedy Profile in Courage Award]] in 2000.

Solis defeated a long-time Democratic incumbent as part of getting elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 2000, where she focused mainly on labor causes and environmental work. She was reelected easily to four subsequent terms. In December 2008, President-elect [[Barack Obama]] announced his intention to nominate Solis as the next Secretary of Labor. She took office after being confirmed by the [[United States Senate]] in February 2009, becoming the first Latina to lead one of the [[United States federal executive departments]]. There she focused on workplace safety issues and on strengthening compliance with wage and hour laws. In January 2013, Solis stepped down from her post as Labor Secretary.

Returning to the area of her upbringing, in April 2014, Solis formally announced a campaign for a seat on the non-partisan [[Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors]]. Solis won the seat outright in a June 3 election and was sworn in on December 1. As Supervisor, Solis successfully lobbied the state to allocate funds for the [[Exide lead contamination|Exide battery plant cleanup]]. One of her areas of responsibility was [[Downtown Los Angeles]], where her main priority was dealing with [[gentrification]] and the lack of [[affordable housing]]. She was unopposed for re-election as Supervisor, which took place in June 2018. She served one-year terms as [[Los Angeles County Chair|county chair]] from 2015 to 2016 and again from 2020 to 2021.

==Early life and education==
Solis was born in [[Los Angeles, California]],<ref name="nj111100"/> as the daughter of immigrant parents who had met in citizenship class and married in 1953: Juana Sequeira (b.&nbsp;1926, from [[Nicaragua]]) and Raúl Solís (from [[Mexico]]).<ref name="lat122800">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-dec-28-me-5513-story.html | title=Solis Prepares to Take Another Step Up | first=Jean|last=Merl| newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=December 28, 2000 | location = Los Angeles, California | access-date=March 12, 2009}}</ref><ref name="cr060606">{{cite web | url=http://bulk.resource.org/gpo.gov/record/2006/2006_E01010.pdf | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090203072027/http://bulk.resource.org/gpo.gov/record/2006/2006_E01010.pdf | url-status=dead | archive-date=February 3, 2009 | title=Honoring Juana Sequeria Solis on Her 80th Birthday | author=Solis, Hilda L. | publisher=[[Congressional Record]] | date=June 6, 2006| access-date=December 22, 2008}}</ref> Her father was a [[Teamsters]] [[Union steward|shop steward]] in Mexico<ref name="wapo121908pre"/> and, after coming to the United States, worked at the Quemetco [[Battery recycling|battery recycling plant]] in the [[Industry, California|City of Industry]] in the [[San Gabriel Valley]].<ref name="svgt010709">{{cite news | url=http://nl.newsbank.com/nl-search/we/Archives?p_product=SGVB&p_theme=sgvb&p_action=search&p_maxdocs=200&s_dispstring=allfields(If%20Rep.%20Hilda%20Solis%20is%20confirmed%20as%20the)%20AND%20date(1/6/2009%20to%201/8/2009)&p_field_date-0=YMD_date&p_params_date-0=date:B,E&p_text_date-0=1/6/2009%20to%201/8/2009&p_field_advanced-0=&p_text_advanced-0=(%22If%20Rep.%20Hilda%20Solis%20is%20confirmed%20as%20the%22)&xcal_numdocs=20&p_perpage=10&p_sort=YMD_date:D&xcal_useweights=no | format=fee required | title=Solis, a woman of many firsts, had a steady rise through California's political ranks | first= Rebecca | last = Kimitch | newspaper=[[San Gabriel Valley Tribune]] | publisher = [[Digital First Media]] | location  = Monrovia, California | date=January 7, 2009 | access-date=January 10, 2009}}</ref> There he again organized for the Teamsters, to gain better health care benefits for workers,<ref name="cq121808"/> but also contracted [[lead poisoning]].<ref name="nyt070509"/> Her mother worked for over 20&nbsp;years on the assembly line of [[Mattel]] once her children were all of school age,<ref name="cr060606"/> belonged to the [[United Rubber Workers]],<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.bloomberg.com/apps/news?pid=20601087&sid=ayIqhZO_UcIQ&refer=home | title=Obama to Name Solis to Labor Post, Kirk as Trade Representative |first1= Kim |last1=Chapman| first2= Mark |last2=Drajem| publisher=[[Bloomberg News]] | date=December 19, 2008| access-date=December 29, 2008}}</ref> and was outspoken about working conditions.<ref name="nyt070509"/> She stressed the importance of education and was a devout [[Roman Catholic]].<ref name="lat122800"/><ref name="cq121808"/> Her Catholic faith, she said, "is a part of my life. My faith is what motivates me."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.ncronline.org/news/labor-secretary-parents-faith-shaped-me|title=Labor secretary: Parents' faith shaped me|date=1 September 2011|accessdate=4 November 2024|author=Zimmerman, Mark|work=National Catholic Reporter}}</ref>

Hilda Solis is the third oldest of seven siblings (four sisters, two brothers) and grew up in a [[tract home]] in [[La Puente, California]].<ref name="lat010909">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/news/printedition/front/la-me-solis9-2009jan09,0,5487953.story | archive-url=https://archive.today/20101117184426/http://www.latimes.com/news/printedition/front/la-me-solis9-2009jan09,0,5487953.story | url-status=dead | archive-date=November 17, 2010 | title=Hilda Solis' belief in unions runs deep |first1=Dan | last1=Morain|first2=Evelyn|last2=Larrubia| newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |location=Los Angeles, California|date=January 9, 2009 | access-date=January 23, 2009}}</ref> She had to help raise her youngest siblings, and later said of her childhood: "It wasn't what you would call the all-American life for a young girl growing up. We had to mature very quickly."<ref name="cq121808"/> She graduated from [[La Puente High School]],<ref name="ca-as">{{cite web|first=Willie|last=Brown|author-link=Willie Brown (politician)|url=http://info.sen.ca.gov/pub/93-94/bill/asm/ab_0001-0050/hr_49_bill_940808_introduced |title=Assembly Resolution No. 49 Relative to commending the Honorable Hilda Solis |publisher=[[California State Assembly]] |date=August 8, 1994 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081222153232/http://info.sen.ca.gov/pub/93-94/bill/asm/ab_0001-0050/hr_49_bill_940808_introduced |archive-date=December 22, 2008 }}</ref> where she saw a lack of support for those wishing to continue their education,<ref name="svgt010709"/> including a [[guidance counselor]] who told her mother that "Your daughter is not college material. Maybe she should follow the career of her older sister and become a secretary."<ref name="nyt070509">{{cite news | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/07/06/us/politics/06solis.html | title=As Labor Secretary, Finding Influence in Her Past | author=Greenhouse, Steven | newspaper=[[The New York Times]] | date=July 5, 2009| access-date=July 7, 2009}}</ref> However, another counselor did encourage her to attend college, and even went to her house to help her fill out an application.<ref name="cq121808">{{cite news|url=http://www.cqpolitics.com/wmspage.cfm?parm1=1&docID=news-000002999241 |title=CQ Politics in America Profile: Hilda Solis |publisher=[[Congressional Quarterly]] |date=June 24, 2010 |access-date=December 22, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090310234112/http://www.cqpolitics.com/wmspage.cfm?parm1=1 |archive-date=March 10, 2009 }}</ref> She took her younger sisters to the library to get them to follow her lead.<ref name="lat010909"/>

She was the first of her family to go to college,<ref name="lat122800"/> being accepted into the Educational Opportunity Program (which assists low-income, first-generation college students) at [[California State Polytechnic University, Pomona]] (Cal Poly Pomona)<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.calstate.edu/SAS/eop/various/alums.shtml |title=EOP ALumni |publisher=[[California State Polytechnic University, Pomona]] |access-date=January 12, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100530105722/http://www.calstate.edu/SAS/eop/various/alums.shtml |archive-date=May 30, 2010 }} and {{cite web|url=http://www.calstate.edu/SAS/eop/various/history.shtml |title=History of EOP |publisher=[[California State Polytechnic University, Pomona]] |access-date=January 12, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20080905035209/http://www.calstate.edu/SAS/eop/various/history.shtml |archive-date=September 5, 2008 }}</ref> and paying for it with the help of government grants and part-time jobs.<ref name="lat122800"/> She graduated in 1979 with a [[Bachelor of Arts]] in [[political science]].<ref name="lat122800"/><ref name="nyt-44-prof">{{cite news | url=http://projects.nytimes.com/44th_president/new_team/show/78 | title=The New Team: Hilda L. Solis | newspaper=[[The New York Times]] | access-date=February 28, 2009 | url-status=dead | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081227022116/http://projects.nytimes.com/44th_president/new_team/show/78 | archive-date=December 27, 2008 | df=mdy-all }}</ref> She then earned a [[Master of Public Administration]] degree at the [[University of Southern California]] in 1981.<ref name="nj111100"/>

==Early career==
Solis served near the end of the [[Carter Administration]] in the White House Office of Hispanic Affairs,<ref name="nj111100"/> where she was editor-in-chief of a newsletter during a 1980–1981 Washington semester internship<ref name="lat122800"/><ref name="cq121808"/><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sen.ca.gov/ftp/SEN/SENATOR__20-__20OLD/SOLIS/PROFILE.BCK |title=Solis, Hilda (D) 24th District |publisher=[[California State Senate]] |access-date=December 22, 2008 }}{{dead link|date=June 2016|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}}</ref> as part of her master's program.<ref name="lat010909"/> At the start of the [[Reagan Administration]] in 1981, she became a [[management analyst]] at the [[civil rights]] division of the [[Office of Management and Budget]], but her dislike for [[Ronald Reagan]]'s policies motivated her to leave later that year.<ref name="cq121808"/><ref name="wt-bio">{{cite news|url=http://www.washingtontimes.com/elections/candidate/541/ |title=Hilda Solis (Dem) |newspaper=[[The Washington Times]] |date=May 5, 2006 |access-date=December 19, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081222161952/http://www.washingtontimes.com/elections/candidate/541/ |archive-date=December 22, 2008 }}</ref>

In Washington, she met Sam H. Sayyad,<ref name="lat010909"/> whom she subsequently married.<!--TODO what year??? --> He owns an automobile repair center in [[Irwindale, California]].<ref name="lat010909"/> The couple lives in a modest house in [[El Monte, California]], not far from where she grew up.<ref name="lat010909"/>

Returning to California, Solis became director of the California Student Opportunity and Access Program in 1982, to help disadvantaged youth gain necessary preparation for college.<ref name="lat122800"/> In particular, she worked with the [[Whittier Union High School District]].<ref name="ca-as"/> Friends urged her to try for elective office,<ref name="nyt070509"/> and so in 1985, she ran for the board of trustees of the [[Rio Hondo College|Rio Hondo Community College]] District.<ref name="lat122800"/> She campaigned hard and overtook an incumbent and one other better established candidate to become the top placer.<ref name="lat122800"/> She was reelected in 1989.<ref name="lat122800"/> During her time on the board, she worked towards improved vocational job training at the college and sought to increase the number of [[Tenure (academic)|tenure]]d faculty positions held by minorities and women.<ref name="svgt010709"/> She joined several California chambers of commerce, women's organizations, and Latino organizations.<ref name="ca-as"/> She gained added political visibility in 1991 when she was named to the Los Angeles County Commission on Insurance by [[Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors|Los Angeles County Supervisor]] [[Gloria Molina]], a political mentor.<ref name="lat122800"/> Solis also served as chief of staff for State Senator [[Arthur Torres|Art Torres]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.wavenewspapers.com/news/local/east-edition/40261552.html |title=Solis Confirmed As Labor Secretary |publisher=[[Los Angeles Wave]] |date=February 25, 2009 |access-date=March 14, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110722142216/http://www.wavenewspapers.com/news/local/east-edition/40261552.html |archive-date=July 22, 2011 }}</ref>

==California State Legislature==
===State Assembly===
Solis had the opportunity to run for the [[California State Assembly]] when, after California's 1991 [[redistricting]], the incumbent Dave Elder<ref name=el90>{{cite web | url=http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/sov/90_gen_sov.pdf | title=Final Results 1990 | publisher=[[California Secretary of State]]|access-date=March 12, 2009 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080730220109/http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/sov/90_gen_sov.pdf |archive-date = July 30, 2008}}</ref> in Solis's [[California's 57th State Assembly district|57th State Assembly district]] was shifted into another district,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sen.ca.gov/reapportionment/HearingTranscripts/10_25_2005.htm |title=Informational Hearing: Instant Runoff and Ranked Choice Elections: Will They Lead to a Better Democracy? |publisher=[[California State Senate]] |date=October 25, 2005 |access-date=December 20, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081222153309/http://www.sen.ca.gov/reapportionment/HearingTranscripts/10_25_2005.htm |archive-date=December 22, 2008 }}</ref> while her new representative retired.<ref name="lat010909"/> In the June 1992 Democratic [[Partisan primary|primary]] to fill the open seat,<ref name="sos-june92"/> Solis's opponents had the endorsement of powerful State Assemblyman [[Richard Polanco]] and the former incumbent.<ref name="lat010909"/> Solis had the support of Molina and U.S. Representative [[Barbara Boxer]], in an effort that focused on door-to-door campaigning<ref name="svgt010709"/> and featured Solis's mother making [[burrito]]s for campaign volunteers.<ref name="lat010909"/> Solis came out on top of a three-way Democratic race, receiving 49&nbsp;percent of the vote and besting her nearest competitor, future State Assemblyman Ed Chavez, who received 31&nbsp;percent.<ref name="sos-june92">{{cite web|url=http://vote96.sos.ca.gov/Vote96/html/stats/SOVp92.htm |title=Statement of Vote, June 2, 1992 |publisher=[[California Secretary of State]] |access-date=March 14, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081026110950/http://vote96.sos.ca.gov/Vote96/html/stats/SOVp92.htm |archive-date=October 26, 2008 }}</ref> In the [[general election]], Solis garnered 61&nbsp;percent of the vote against Republican Gary Woods's 34&nbsp;percent, and gained election to the State Assembly.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://sos.ca.gov/elections/sov/1992_general/statement_of_vote_general_1992.pdf | title=Final Results 1992 | publisher=[[California Secretary of State]] | access-date=March 12, 2009 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080730215019/http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/sov/1992_general/statement_of_vote_general_1992.pdf |archive-date = July 30, 2008}}</ref> She was one of seven Latinos who won election to the State Assembly in the wake of the redistricting and became collectively known as ''Los Siete''.<ref name="acuna"/> Solis was among the most liberal of this ideologically diverse group.<ref name="acuna">{{cite book | last=Acuña | first=Rodolfo | title=Anything But Mexican: Chicanos in Contemporary Los Angeles | url=https://archive.org/details/anythingbutmexic00acu | url-access=registration | publisher=[[Verso Books]] | year=1996 | isbn=1-85984-031-0 | page=[https://archive.org/details/anythingbutmexic00acu/page/97 97]}}</ref>

In her one term in the State Assembly, Solis was prominent in the debate on [[illegal immigration to the United States]], backing a bill to allow immigrants in the United States illegally to attend California colleges as long as they were residing in the state.<ref name="svgt010709"/> She backed labor unions and opposed the tobacco industry in supporting a bill that banned smoking in all workplaces.<ref name="lat010909"/> She served on committees dealing with education, labor, and environmental issues, including a new committee that dealt with groundwater contamination and landfill leakage.<ref name="svgt010709"/> She was not known as a strong orator.<ref name="lat010909"/>

===State Senate===
The Democratic incumbent in Solis's [[California's 24th State Senate district|24th State Senate district]], [[Arthur Torres|Art Torres]],<ref name=el90/> gave up his office when he received the 1994 Democratic nomination for the statewide office of [[California Insurance Commissioner]].<ref name=el94/> Solis ran for the seat, won the Democratic primary with 63&nbsp;percent of the vote against two opponents,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://vote96.sos.ca.gov/Vote96/html/stats/SOVp94.htm |title=Statement of Vote '94 |date=June 3, 1994 |publisher=[[California Secretary of State]] |access-date=December 20, 2008 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081222153313/http://vote96.sos.ca.gov/Vote96/html/stats/SOVp94.htm |archive-date=December 22, 2008 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> and then won the 1994 general election with 63&nbsp;percent of the vote against Republican Dave Boyer's 33&nbsp;percent.<ref name=el94>{{cite web | url=http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/sov/1994_general/sov_94_gen_complete.pdf | title=Statement of Vote | date=November 8, 1994 | publisher=[[California Secretary of State]] | access-date=December 20, 2008 |archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20080730213903/http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/sov/1994_general/sov_94_gen_complete.pdf |archive-date = July 30, 2008}}</ref> She became the first Hispanic woman to ever serve in the State Senate and the first woman ever to represent the San Gabriel Valley;<ref name="svgt010709"/> she was also the Senate's youngest member at that time.<ref name="cq121808"/> She was reelected in 1998 with 74&nbsp;percent of the vote.<ref name=el98>{{cite web|url=http://vote98.sos.ca.gov/Final/sov/SOV35-37.pdf |title=State Senator |publisher=[[California Secretary of State]] |access-date=March 12, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090325021004/http://vote98.sos.ca.gov/Final/sov/SOV35-37.pdf |archive-date=March 25, 2009 |df=mdy-all }}</ref>

In the State Senate, Solis authored 17&nbsp;bills to prevent [[domestic violence]]<ref name="nyt-44-prof"/> and championed labor, education, and health care issues.<ref name="lat122800"/> She described herself as "a big believer that government, if done right, can do a lot to improve the quality of people's lives".<ref name="lat122800"/> In 1995, she sponsored a bill to raise the [[minimum wage]] from $4.25 to $5.75; it was strongly opposed by business organizations and the restaurant industry.<ref name="lat122800"/><ref name="svgt010709"/> When Governor [[Pete Wilson]] vetoed it, she organized a successful drive to make the issue into a [[Popular initiative|ballot initiative]] the next year, using $50,000 of her own campaign funds and rallying union support.<ref name="lat122800"/><ref name="cj120101">{{cite news|url=http://www.house.gov/apps/list/press/ca32_solis/morenews4/cajournal.html |title=Hilda Solis: Profile in Courage |author=Rodriguez, Emelyn |publisher=[[California Journal]] |date=December 1, 2001 |access-date=March 14, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070812102638/http://www.house.gov/apps/list/press/ca32_solis/morenews4/cajournal.html |archive-date=August 12, 2007 }}</ref> The initiative's passing garnered her a statewide reputation<ref name="pol011309">{{cite news | url=https://www.politico.com/story/2009/01/department-of-labor-hilda-l-solis-017253 | title=Department of Labor: Hilda L. Solis | author=Lerer, Lisa | publisher=[[Politico]] | date=January 13, 2009| access-date=January 14, 2009}}</ref> and other states followed with similar initiatives.<ref name="lat010909"/> She chaired the labor committee and established herself as loyal to labor interests, but made a point of establishing working relationships with [[Republican Party (United States)|Republicans]] on the committee.<ref name="lat010909"/> Solis held high-profile hearings on labor law enforcement following a summer 1995 [[sweatshop]] raid in El Monte that discovered more than 70 [[Thai people|Thai]] workers existing in [[slavery|slave]]-like conditions.<ref name="lat010909"/> She called garment manufacturers to explain themselves and pushed for tougher enforcement of [[anti-sweatshop]] laws.<ref name="lat010909"/> Republican state senator [[Ray Haynes]] later said that Solis was "a committed liberal in the pockets of labor", but Republican State Senate Leader [[Rob Hurtt]] said of her, "We obviously didn't see eye to eye. But she was respectful. I'll give her credit; she was a very hard worker and she knew her stuff."<ref name="lat010909"/>

Solis was an environmental activist in the State Senate, due to concerns that stemmed from a childhood spent within smelling distance of the [[Puente Hills Landfill]]<ref name="lat010909"/> and making frequent visits to the [[San Gabriel Mountains]].<ref name="lat021704">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/science/la-os-solis17feb17-story.html | title=L.A.'s Wild Fringe | author=Sullivan, Susan | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=February 17, 2004 | access-date=December 19, 2008}}</ref> In 1997, she worked to pass [[environmental justice]] legislation with a law to protect low-income and minority communities from newly located landfills, pollution sources, and other environmental hazards in neighborhoods that already had such sites.<ref name="lat060200">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-jun-02-mn-36591-story.html | title=Ethics Law Bars Solis From Keeping Courage Award | author=Ingram, Carl | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=June 2, 2000 | access-date=March 12, 2009}}</ref> She got the bill, SB 1113, approved over the strong opposition of various business interests, water contractors, and some state government agencies, but Wilson vetoed it.<ref name="lat060200"/> She returned in 1999 with a compromise measure, which was signed by Governor [[Gray Davis]].<ref name="lat060200"/> Calling for "the fair treatment of people of all races, cultures, and incomes with respect to the development, adoption, implementation, and enforcement of environmental laws",<ref name="jfk052200"/> it represented the first legislation of its kind in the nation and is considered a landmark.<ref name="lat122800"/><ref name="nyt070509"/>

Solis faced controversy with her 1999 legislation, SB&nbsp;63, that lowered the carpool restrictions on the [[El Monte Busway]] from three or more occupants to two or more.<ref name="its2002">{{cite web | url=http://www.itsdocs.fhwa.dot.gov/JPODOCS/REPTS_TE/13692.html | title=Effects of Changing HOV Lane Occupancy Requirements: El Monte Busway Case Study | work=Intelligent Transportation Systems | publisher=[[United States Department of Transportation]] | date=June 2002 | access-date=March 14, 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090320050341/http://www.itsdocs.fhwa.dot.gov//JPODOCS/REPTS_TE//13692.html <!--Added by H3llBot--> | archive-date=March 20, 2009}}</ref><ref name="lat012200"/> When this took effect in January 2000, it quickly resulted in greatly increased volume on the busway and protests from bus riders and prior carpoolers.<ref name="lat012200">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-jan-22-mn-56559-story.html | title=Easing of Carpool Rules Backfires as Lanes Jam | author=Shuit, Douglas P. | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=January 22, 2000 | access-date=March 14, 2009}}</ref> Solis at first defended the change,<ref name="lat012200"/> but it continued to have a detrimental effect on the busway and did not improve flow in the regular traffic lanes.<ref name="its2002"/><ref name="lat051700"/>  By May, she was co-sponsoring legislation to rescind the change and restore the higher occupancy requirement,<ref name="lat051700">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2000-may-17-me-31101-story.html | title=Bill to Restore El Monte Busway Moves Forward | author=Shuit, Douglas P. | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=May 17, 2000 | access-date=March 14, 2009}}</ref> which passed and took effect in July 2000.<ref name="its2002"/>

Due to her work in overcoming obstacles for environmental justice, in 2000 Solis was given the [[Profile in Courage Award]] by the [[John F. Kennedy Library Foundation]], and was praised as "a politician who hasn't shied away from challenging the old boy network both within and without the Latino community".<ref name="jfk052200">{{cite press release | url=http://www.jfklibrary.org/Education+and+Public+Programs/Profile+in+Courage+Award/Award+Recipients/Hilda+Solis/Award+Announcement.htm | title=California State Senator Hilda Solis Receives 2000 John F. Kennedy Profile in Courage Award | publisher=[[John F. Kennedy Library Foundation]] | date=May 22, 2000 | access-date=December 19, 2008 | archive-date=March 1, 2009 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090301024152/http://www.jfklibrary.org/Education+and+Public+Programs/Profile+in+Courage+Award/Award+Recipients/Hilda+Solis/Award+Announcement.htm | url-status=dead }}</ref> She was the first woman to win the award,<ref name="aap-08"/> and gained appearances in ''[[George (magazine)|George]]'' and ''[[People (magazine)|People]]'' magazines and on the ''[[Today (NBC program)|Today]]'' show.<ref name="lat122800"/> Art Torres, who had become [[California Democratic Party]] chair, said of Solis, "She's going to be a national star".<ref name="lat122800"/>

==U.S. House of Representatives==
[[Image:Hilda Solis, official photo portrait, color.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Solis' official portrait, as it appeared on her Congressional website in 2003]]
Term limits would have prevented Solis from seeking reelection to the State Senate.<ref name="wt-bio"/> After months of deliberation, she decided to run for the U.S. House of Representatives in 2000 against 18-year incumbent [[Matthew G. Martínez]] in the [[California's 31st congressional district|31st congressional district]], which consisted largely of working class Hispanics and [[Asian people|Asians]].<ref name="lat122800"/> This action was criticized by Hispanics and others, and only two members of Congress, [[Barbara Boxer]] and [[Loretta Sanchez]], supported her.<ref name="cq121808"/><ref name="nyt070509"/> Martínez was more moderate than many of his constituents, as he had supported the [[North American Free Trade Agreement]] (NAFTA), opposed [[Gun politics|gun control]], and supported bans on specific [[abortion]] procedures.<ref name="nj111100">{{cite news |title=Biographies. |url=http://www.accessmylibrary.com/coms2/summary_0286-28655161_ITM |work=National Journal |date=November 11, 2000 |access-date=December 19, 2008}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |first=Harold |last=Meyerson |title=Labor's fresh face |url=https://www.latimes.com/news/opinion/commentary/la-oe-meyerson19-2008dec19,0,5862785.story |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=December 19, 2008 |access-date=December 19, 2008}}</ref>  He was also criticized for lacking effort and neglecting his district.<ref name="lat122800"/> Solis was able to obtain the support of the Los Angeles County Federation of Labor (which called her a "warrior for working families"),<ref name="nyt070509"/> [[Emily's List]], [[Brady Campaign|Handgun Control Incorporation]], the [[Sierra Club]] and the [[California League of Conservation Voters]].  With their help, Solis outspent Martínez by a 4-to-1 margin and had hundreds of volunteers working for her.<ref name="aap-08">{{cite book |title = The Almanac of American Politics |last = Barone |first = Michael |author-link = Michael Barone (pundit) |author2 = Cohen, Richard E. |author-link2 = Richard E. Cohen |year = 2008 |publisher = National Journal Group |location = Washington |isbn = 978-0892341177 |pages = [https://archive.org/details/almanacofamerica00mich_0/page/247 247–249] |url-access = registration |url = https://archive.org/details/almanacofamerica00mich_0/page/247 }}</ref>

Solis defeated Martínez in the March 2000 Democratic primary by a 69&nbsp;percent to 31&nbsp;percent margin.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/sov/2000_primary/us_rep.pdf |title=Statement of Vote 2000 Primary Election: Representatives in Congress |publisher=[[California Secretary of State]] |access-date=March 14, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070612144846/http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/sov/2000_primary/us_rep.pdf |archive-date=June 12, 2007 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> On primary night, Martínez called Solis "obnoxious" and accused her of untruthful advertising.<ref name="nj111100"/> He subsequently switched to the [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican Party]], and urged Latinos to vote against her, to no great effect.<ref name="aap-08"/> Without a Republican opponent in the general election, Solis beat three little-known challengers from [[Third party (United States)|minor parties]] and won 79&nbsp;percent of the vote.<ref name="lat122800"/>

[[File:SolisPharmacistsAppearance.jpg|thumb|right|Solis at a 2006 appearance with local pharmacists concerned with [[Medicare Part D]] implementation]]
Upon arriving in the House of Representatives, Solis was named freshman class [[Whip (politics)|whip]], making her responsible for collecting votes from first-term Democrats.<ref name="cj120101"/>  ''[[National Journal]]'' magazine named her one of its "Ten Freshmen to Watch", and said that her election "is a sign of things to come in California and a generational changing of the guard in the [[Hispanic Caucus]]".<ref name="cj120101"/>  Solis commissioned for her new office a painting of the [[United States Capitol]] with the [[San Gabriel Mountains]] behind it, so that she would not forget her roots.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.usnews.com/articles/news/obama/2009/02/13/10-things-you-didnt-know-about-hilda-solis.html |title=10 Things You Didn't Know About Hilda Solis |author=Burton, Danielle |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |date=February 13, 2009 |access-date=February 13, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090216010953/http://www.usnews.com/articles/news/obama/2009/02/13/10-things-you-didnt-know-about-hilda-solis.html |archive-date=February 16, 2009 }}</ref> Her Washington apartment was tiny.<ref name="nyt070509"/>

As congresswoman, Solis was most known for her work on environmental issues as a member of the [[United States House Committee on Energy and Commerce|Committee on Energy and Commerce]], the [[United States House Committee on Natural Resources|Committee on Natural Resources]], and the [[United States House Select Committee on Energy Independence and Global Warming|Select Committee on Energy Independence and Global Warming]].<ref name="wapo121908pre"/> She made the promotion of [[Green-collar worker|green-collar jobs]] a priority<ref name="wapo121908pre"/> and sponsored the Southern California portion of the California Wild Heritage Act, which would create or enlarge many wilderness areas.<ref name="lat021704"/> In 2003, she sponsored legislation that funded a [[National Park Service]] study to designate a large swath of the [[Angeles National Forest]], the [[Puente Hills|Puente]] and [[Chino Hills]], and the [[Rio Hondo (California)|Rio Hondo]] and [[San Gabriel River (California)|San Gabriel River]], a [[National Recreation Area]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.sgvtribune.com/news/ci_22684531/national-park-status-san-gabriel-mountains-river-reach?IADID=Search-www.sgvtribune.com-www.sgvtribune.com | archive-url=https://archive.today/20130630082105/http://www.sgvtribune.com/news/ci_22684531/national-park-status-san-gabriel-mountains-river-reach?IADID=Search-www.sgvtribune.com-www.sgvtribune.com | url-status=dead | archive-date=June 30, 2013 | title=National Park status for San Gabriel Mountains, river reach White House budget office | author=Scauzillo, Steve | newspaper=[[San Gabriel Valley Tribune]] | date=February 27, 2013 | access-date=April 17, 2013 }}</ref>  (In 2013, after Solis had left the Obama administration, the Park Service recommended proceeding with a greatly reduced version of the original proposal; while other advocates evinced disappointment, Solis said it was still a positive step and that Congress could expand the area in whatever legislation it undertook.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.sgvtribune.com/news/ci_22999201/national-park-service-recommends-scaled-down-recreation-area | title=National Park Service recommends scaled down recreation area for San Gabriel River, Puente Hills | author=Scauzillo, Steve | newspaper=[[San Gabriel Valley Tribune]] | date=April 11, 2013 | access-date=April 17, 2013}}</ref>)

Solis was not a member of the [[United States House Committee on Education and the Workforce|Education and the Workforce Committee]], but championed the [[Employee Free Choice Act]]<ref name="nyt121908"/> and was the only member of Congress on the board of [[American Rights at Work]], a pro-union organization that strongly supports the act, for whom she served as treasurer starting in 2004.<ref name="nyt121908"/><ref name="wsj020209">{{cite news | url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB123350459826036791 | title=Daschle Faces Questions on Trips |author1=Weisman, Jonathan  |author2=Trottman, Melanie | newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]] | date=February 2, 2009 | access-date=February 2, 2009}}</ref> On trade she voted against both the [[Dominican Republic – Central America Free Trade Agreement|Dominican Republic–Central America trade agreement]]<ref>{{cite web | url=http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2005/roll443.xml | title=Final Vote Results for Roll Call 443 | publisher=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives]] | date=July 28, 2005 | access-date=March 12, 2009}}</ref> and the [[United States – Peru Trade Promotion Agreement|U.S.-Peru trade agreement]],<ref>{{cite web | url=http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2007/roll1060.xml | title=Final Vote Results for Roll Call 1060| publisher=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives]] | date=November 8, 2007 | access-date=March 12, 2009}}</ref> and also expressed opposition to a purposed bilateral [[United States-Colombia Free Trade Agreement|U.S.-Colombia trade agreement]], citing concerns about human rights violations.<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://solis.house.gov/list/speech/ca32_solis/wida6/colombiafta41008.shtml |title=Solis Statement on Colombia Free Trade Agreement |publisher=Hilda L. Solis Congressional Website |date=April 10, 2008 |access-date=March 12, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090130012649/http://solis.house.gov/list/speech/ca32_solis/wida6/colombiafta41008.shtml |archive-date=January 30, 2009 }}</ref> Solis opposed legislation that would soften job safety requirements.<ref name="pol121808"/> She received 100&nbsp;percent ratings from several pro-labor groups for the years 2005 through 2007,<ref name="lat121908">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/news/nationworld/nation/la-na-solis19-2008dec19,0,9325.story | title=Obama to name pro-union Rep. Hilda Solis to Labor post | author=Nicholas, Peter | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=December 19, 2008 | access-date=December 19, 2008}}</ref> and was a major recipient of union political donations.<ref name="pol011309"/> [[United Farm Workers]] co-founder [[Dolores Huerta]] is one of Solis's role models.<ref name="pol011309"/>

[[Image:SanGabrielRiverSiteDedication.jpg|thumb|upright|left|Solis (third from left) at a 2006 dedication ceremony for a conservation land acquisition along the [[San Gabriel River (California)|San Gabriel River]]]]
During her tenure in the House, Solis was an advocate of comprehensive immigration reform. She was one of the leading opponents of [[Border Protection, Anti-terrorism, and Illegal Immigration Control Act of 2005|H.R. 4437]] a House bill sponsored by Wisconsin Congressman [[Jim Sensenbrenner]] and voted against it.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://clerk.house.gov/evs/2005/roll661.xml | title=Final Vote Results for Roll Call 661 | publisher=[[Clerk of the United States House of Representatives]] | date=December 16, 2005 | access-date=March 12, 2009}}</ref>

Solis supported legislation aimed at reducing the number of [[Teenage pregnancy|teen pregnancies]] within [[Hispanic and Latino Americans|Latina]] and [[African American]] communities<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.house.gov/apps/list/speech/ca32_solis/TeenPregnancyPreventionBillIntro.html |title=Solis Introduces Teen Pregnancy Prevention Bill |access-date=December 19, 2008 |date=July 14, 2006 |publisher=[[United States House of Representatives]] |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081222150302/http://www.house.gov/apps/list/speech/ca32_solis/TeenPregnancyPreventionBillIntro.html |archive-date=December 22, 2008 }}</ref> and sponsored a bill, that became law in 2003, that granted U.S.&nbsp;citizenship to immigrants after one year of military service instead of the previous three years.<ref name="wapo121908pre"/>

Solis is [[Roman Catholic Church|Roman Catholic]] and [[pro-choice]].<ref name="c-sop"/> Along with 47 other Catholic members of Congress, she sent a letter to Cardinal [[Theodore Edgar McCarrick|Theodore McCarrick]] of [[Washington, D.C.]], in order to dissuade him from refusing them the [[sacraments]] because of their pro-choice legislative voting.<ref>{{cite news|last=Woodward|first=Kenneth&nbsp;L.|title=A Political Sacrament|newspaper=[[The New York Times]]|date=May 28, 2008|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9F04E1DE103EF93BA15756C0A9629C8B63|access-date=March 12, 2009}}</ref> Solis signed a "Statement of Principles," stating her commitment to her faith as well as her disagreement with the Roman Catholic Church on some issues.<ref name="c-sop">{{Cite web |url=http://delauro.house.gov/release.cfm?id=1206 |title=House Democrats Release Historic Catholic Statement of Principles |access-date=December 19, 2008 |date=February 28, 2006 |publisher=Congresswoman Rosa L. DeLauro |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120218121902/http://delauro.house.gov/release.cfm?id=1206 |archive-date=February 18, 2012 |df=mdy-all }}</ref> They stated that on those issues, such as abortion rights, they decided to follow their conscience instead of the Church teachings.<ref name="c-sop"/>

Solis was a member of the [[Congressional Progressive Caucus]]<ref name="cq121808"/> and rated a lifetime "liberal quotient" of 99&nbsp;percent from [[Americans for Democratic Action]],<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.adaction.org/pages/publications/voting-records.php | title=Voting Records | publisher=[[Americans for Democratic Action]] | access-date=March 1, 2009 | archive-date=August 30, 2017 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170830205034/http://www.adaction.org/pages/publications/voting-records.php | url-status=dead }} Scores for years 2001 through 2007 were 100, for 2008 was 95 due to a missed vote.</ref> and a lifetime 2&nbsp;percent rating from the [[American Conservative Union]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.conservative.org/ratings/ratingsarchive/2008/2008house.htm |title=2008 U.S. House Votes |publisher=[[American Conservative Union]] |access-date=March 20, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100831044420/http://www.conservative.org/ratings/ratingsarchive/2008/2008house.htm |archive-date=August 31, 2010 }} Lifetime averages are given.</ref> From 2006 to 2008 she wrote blog entries for [[The Huffington Post]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/rep-hilda-l-solis | title=Rep. Hilda L. Solis | work=[[HuffPost]] | access-date=December 22, 2008}}</ref> Solis believed in the importance of [[Mentorship|mentoring]], and as a House member continued relationships she had established with up-and-coming political figures in her district, including California State Assemblywoman [[Judy Chu]] and [[Monterey Park, California|Monterey Park]] Mayor Sharon Martinez.<ref>{{cite book | last=Ensher | first=Ellen A. |author2=Murphy, Susan E. | title=Power Mentoring: How Successful Mentors and Protégés Get the Most Out of Their Relationships | publisher=[[John Wiley and Sons]] | year=2005 | isbn=0-7879-7952-X | pages=91–93}}</ref>

[[Image:Hilda Solis.jpg|thumb|right|upright|Solis's official Congressional portrait, 2007]]
After the 2000 census and subsequent redistricting, Solis's area became part of [[California's 32nd congressional district]]. She was reelected for additional terms in 2002, 2004, and 2006 by very large margins, twice with no Republican in opposition.<ref name="cq121808"/> She ran unopposed in 2008.<ref name=el08>{{cite web|url=http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/sov/2008_general/23_34_us_reps.pdf |title=United States Representative |publisher=[[California Secretary of State]] |access-date=March 12, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081221042514/http://www.sos.ca.gov/elections/sov/2008_general/23_34_us_reps.pdf |archive-date=December 21, 2008 }}</ref>
Solis chaired the Health and the Environment Task Force of the [[Congressional Hispanic Caucus]] during the [[110th United States Congress|110th Congress]].<ref>{{cite press release | url=http://roybal-allard.house.gov/News/DocumentSingle.aspx?DocumentID=126422 | title=The Congressional Hispanic Caucus (CHC) Applauded President-elect Obama's Nomination of Congresswoman Hilda L. Solis for Secretary of Labor | publisher=[[Congressional Hispanic Caucus]] | date=December 19, 2008 | access-date=September 10, 2009}}</ref> However, during 2006 and 2007, Solis was part of a falling out between several female representatives and [[Joe Baca]], leader of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, arguing there was a "lack of respect afforded to women members of the Hispanic Caucus," which Baca denied.<ref name="cq121808"/> She had previously broken ties with the caucus' [[political action committee]] over its campaign contributions to Baca's sons.<ref name="wapo022207"/> Baca responded that Solis "was a kiss-up" to House Speaker [[Nancy Pelosi]], a remark for which he later apologized.<ref name="wapo022207">{{cite news | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2007/02/21/AR2007022101772.html | title=Women Call for Change in Caucus | author=Layton, Lyndsey | newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] | date=February 22, 2007 | access-date=January 4, 2009}}</ref> Solis was indeed considered a close ally of Pelosi,<ref name="nyt121908"/> which helped her get a seat on the Energy and Commerce Committee.<ref name="cq121808"/> She considered running for the position of [[Democratic Caucus Vice-Chairman of the United States House of Representatives|Democratic Caucus Vice-Chairman]] for the [[110th United States Congress|110th Congress]], but deferred to incumbent [[John B. Larson|John Larson]] after [[Rahm Emanuel]] chose to run for caucus chair, which Larson had been running for.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://kendrickmeek.us/ShowPage.asp%3Fpage%3DTheHill11102006.asp |title=House Dems strike leadership deal |author=Hearn, Josephine |newspaper=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |date=November 10, 2006 |access-date=March 14, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081127024927/http://www.kendrickmeek.us/ShowPage.asp?page=TheHill11102006.asp |archive-date=November 27, 2008 }}</ref> Solis's aggressive fundraising for the [[Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee]] gained her a vice chair position on the [[Steering and Policy Committee of the United States House of Representatives|Democratic Steering & Policy Committee]].<ref name="cq121808"/> At the time of her selection to Obama's cabinet, she had been elected 2nd vice chair of the Hispanic Caucus<ref>{{cite press release|url=http://www.house.gov/apps/list/press/ca38_napolitano/morenews/pr111908.html |title=Hispanic Caucus Elects Leadership for the 111th Congress |publisher=[[Congressional Hispanic Caucus]] |date=November 19, 2008 |access-date=September 10, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091008183807/http://www.house.gov/apps/list/press/ca38_napolitano/morenews/pr111908.html |archive-date=October 8, 2009 }}</ref> and was considered a potential candidate for a leadership position in the House.<ref name="pol121808">{{cite news | url=https://www.politico.com/story/2008/12/labor-ties-drive-solis-pick-016730 | title=Labor ties drive Solis pick |author1=O'Connor, Patrick  |author2=Parnes, Amie | publisher=[[Politico]] | date=December 18, 2008 | access-date=December 24, 2008}}</ref>

Solis was a strong supporter of [[Hillary Clinton]]'s [[Hillary Clinton 2008 presidential campaign|2008 presidential bid]]; when that fell short, [[Barack Obama]] aggressively sought her support, as part of strengthening his appeal to Hispanic voters.<ref name="wapo121908pre"/> She supported Clinton's effort to establish a [[United States Public Service Academy|U.S. Public Service Academy]] and was a co-sponsor of a House bill to create one.<ref>{{cite web|title=H.R.1671|publisher=[[Library of Congress]]|url=http://thomas.loc.gov/cgi-bin/bdquery/z?d110:HR01671:@@@P|access-date=March 12, 2009|archive-date=October 18, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151018231328/http://thomas.loc.gov/cgi-bin/bdquery/z?d110:HR01671:@@@P|url-status=dead}}</ref> Solis did not become wealthy from her political career; by 2008, she and her husband's main assets consisted of retirement funds and his auto shop, valued at under $100,000.<ref name="lat010909"/>

==U.S. Secretary of Labor==
[[File:SolisObamaSecLaborAnnouncement.jpg|thumb|right|Solis speaks at the announcement of her being chosen as the new Secretary of Labor. President-elect [[Barack Obama]] and [[United States Trade Representative]]-to-be [[Ron Kirk]] look on.]]
On December 18, 2008, sources close to the [[Presidential transition of Barack Obama|Obama transition team]] identified Solis as the President-elect's choice for [[United States Secretary of Labor|Secretary of Labor]], the last cabinet position yet to be filled.<ref>{{cite news |title=AP source: Rep. Hilda Solis is Obama's labor pick |url=https://www.usatoday.com/news/politics/2008-12-18-obama-solis-labor_N.htm |agency=[[Associated Press]] |work=[[USA Today]] |date=December 19, 2008 |access-date=March 12, 2008}}</ref> The selection earned praise from the [[AFL-CIO]] and other labor organizations, but was not well received by business groups<ref name="nyt121908">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2008/12/19/us/politics/19obama.html |title=Picks for Labor and Trade Positions Disagree on Policy |author1=Cooper, Helene  |author2=Greenhouse, Steven |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=December 19, 2008 |access-date=December 19, 2008}}</ref> and the anti-union group [[Center for Union Facts]].<ref name="wapo121908pre">{{cite news |first=Anne&nbsp;E. |last=Kornblut |title=Obama to Announce Final Cabinet Picks |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2008/12/18/AR2008121804057.html |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=December 19, 2008 |access-date=March 12, 2008}}</ref> The official announcement was made by Obama on December 19.<ref name="wapo121908pre" /> Solis's successor was chosen in a [[California's 32nd congressional district special election, 2009|special election in California's 32nd congressional district]]; she declined to endorse a candidate in the primary<ref name="lat012909">{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/news/local/politics/cal/la-me-chu29-2009jan29,0,3122857.story |title=L.A. County Federation of Labor endorses Chu for Congress |author=Larrubia, Evelyn |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=January 29, 2009 |access-date=January 29, 2009}}</ref> (from which her past mentee [[Judy Chu]] emerged on top and eventually won the general election).<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.pasadenastarnews.com/ci_12839817 |title=Judy Chu wins 32nd Congressional District race |author=Kimitch, Rebecca |newspaper=[[Pasadena Star-News]] |date=July 14, 2009 |access-date=July 15, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090716131617/http://www.pasadenastarnews.com/ci_12839817 |archive-date=July 16, 2009}}</ref>
[[File:Solis arrival at DOL 1.jpg|thumb|left|Secretary Solis is greeted on her first day of work at the [[Frances Perkins Building]].]]
Solis's confirmation hearings were held on January 9, 2009, before the [[United States Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions|Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee]].<ref name="nyt010909">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/01/10/us/10labor.html |title=With Senate Hearing, Preparing for Change at Top of Labor Dept. |author=Greenhouse, Steven |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=January 9, 2009 |access-date=January 10, 2009}}</ref> Committee chair [[Ted Kennedy]] repeatedly praised her, while, despite examination by Republican members, Solis declined to discuss specific policy issues, including the [[Employee Free Choice Act]].<ref name="nyt010909" /> Several days later, Senate Republicans said they might try to put a procedural hold on her nomination because of her unwillingness to answer questions in detail in the hearings.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2009/01/gop-ers-may-block-solis-confirmation-017538 |title=GOP-ers may block Solis confirmation |author=Raju, Manu |publisher=[[Politico]] |date=January 16, 2009 |access-date=January 18, 2009}}</ref> By January 23, a [[secret hold]] was placed on the nomination by an anonymous Republican.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.govexec.com/dailyfed/0109/012309cdam1.htm |title=Solis becomes latest nominee slowed by GOP roadblocks |author=Friedman, Dan |publisher=[[CongressDaily]] |date=January 23, 2009 |access-date=January 23, 2009 |archive-date=January 29, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090129085535/http://govexec.com/dailyfed/0109/012309cdam1.htm |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/news/nationworld/nation/la-na-nominees30-2009jan30,0,5539680.story |title=Labor nominee Hilda Solis hits GOP roadblock |author=Nicholas, Peter |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=January 30, 2009 |access-date=January 30, 2009}}</ref> A series of written questions and responses between Republican members and Solis followed, during which she was more forthcoming.<ref name="lat020509">{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/news/nationworld/nation/la-na-solis5-2009feb05,0,4387613.story |title=Republicans want Labor nominee to stop lobbying for 'card check' bill |author=Nicholas, Peter |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=February 5, 2009 |access-date=February 5, 2009}}</ref> Republican [[Mike Enzi]] pressed her on whether her unpaid high-level positions at American Rights at Work constituted prohibited lobbying activity; Solis denied violation of rules of conduct and stated she had not helped lobbying.<ref name="wsj020209" /><ref name="lat020509" /> Solis did acknowledge that she had failed to report those positions on her annual House financial disclosure forms at the time, which a White House spokesperson argued was an unintentional oversight.<ref name="lat020509" /> On February 2, Obama appointed veteran Labor Department official [[Edward C. Hugler]] as Acting Secretary.<ref name="wapo020509">{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/story/2009/02/04/ST2009020403880.html |title=After Delay, Panel to Vote on Solis Nomination |author=Fletcher, Michael A. |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=February 5, 2009 |access-date=February 5, 2009}}</ref> The prolonged process was considered by some Republican aides to be a preview of future battles on labor issues between the Obama administration and Republicans in Congress.<ref name="wapo020509" />

[[File:Hilda Solis Secrétaire au travail.jpg|thumb|right|upright=0.75|Official portrait as Secretary of Labor, 2009]]

A vote on Solis's committee confirmation was set on February 5, but postponed after news that Solis's husband Sam Sayyad had just paid $6,400 in outstanding state and local tax liens dating back to 1993 for his auto repair business.<ref name="usa020509"/><ref>{{cite news |url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/44/2009/02/05/solis_senate_session_canceled.html |archive-url=https://archive.today/20120715143211/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/44/2009/02/05/solis_senate_session_canceled.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=July 15, 2012 |title=Solis Senate Session Postponed in Wake of Husband's Tax Lien Revelations |author=Fletcher, Michael A. |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=February 5, 2009 |access-date=February 5, 2009}}</ref> Sayyad had filed a separate tax return from Solis, and intended to contest the lien as they were for business taxes he believed to have already paid.<ref name="pol021009"/> A White House spokesperson stated Solis should not be penalized for any mistakes that her husband may have made.<ref name="usa020509">{{cite news |url=https://www.usatoday.com/news/washington/2009-02-05-solis-husband-taxes_N.htm |title=Tax snafus add up for Obama team |author=Kelley, Matt |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |date=February 5, 2009 |access-date=February 5, 2009}}</ref> The revelations came in the wake of several other Obama nominations troubled or derailed due to tax issues.<ref name="usa020509"/> Committee Republicans subsequently indicated they would not blame Solis, but were still concerned about her ties to American Rights at Work.<ref name="pol021009">{{cite news |url=https://www.politico.com/story/2009/02/gop-wont-derail-solis-on-hubby-018672 |title=GOP won't derail Solis on hubby's taxes |author=Raju, Manu |publisher=[[Politico]] |date=February 10, 2009 |access-date=February 10, 2009}}</ref> On February 11, 2009, the committee approved her nomination by voice vote with two votes opposed.<ref>{{cite news |last=Hananel |first=Sam |title=Senate panel approves labor nominee Hilda Solis |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 11, 2009 |url=https://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5hKhB0orH1HqnAzOkQ_fDe9HNNLqAD969LHVO0 |access-date=March 12, 2009 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090215201601/http://www.google.com/hostednews/ap/article/ALeqM5hKhB0orH1HqnAzOkQ_fDe9HNNLqAD969LHVO0 |archive-date=February 15, 2009 |url-status=dead |df=mdy}}</ref> After still further delays, Republicans agreed not to subject her nomination to a [[filibuster]] and on February 24, 2009, Solis was confirmed by the Senate by a vote of 80–17.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://voices.washingtonpost.com/44/2009/02/24/solis_cleared_for_senate_confi.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120112212416/http://voices.washingtonpost.com/44/2009/02/24/solis_cleared_for_senate_confi.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 12, 2012 |title=Solis Cleared for Senate Confirmation Later Today |author=Fletcher, Michael A. |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=February 24, 2009 |access-date=February 24, 2009}}</ref> She resigned from the House and was sworn into her new position that evening.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.cqpolitics.com/wmspage.cfm?parm1=5&docID=news-000003059528 |title=Senate Confirms Solis as Labor Secretary Despite GOP Concerns |author=Demirjian, Karoun |work=[[Congressional Quarterly]] |date=February 24, 2009 |access-date=February 24, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090224144340/http://www.cqpolitics.com/wmspage.cfm?parm1=5 |archive-date=February 24, 2009}}</ref> (A ceremonial swearing in featuring Vice President [[Joe Biden]] was later held on March 13.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.rttnews.com/ArticleView.aspx?Id=882255&SMap=1&pageNum=2574_2858_1 |title=Solis Formally Sworn in as Labor Secretary |publisher=RTT News |date=March 13, 2009 |access-date=March 17, 2009}}</ref>)

[[Image:Phil Schiliro, Kevin Stricklin, Joe Main, Greg Wagner, Barack Obama, and Hilda L. Solis, 2010.jpg|thumb|left|President Obama, Secretary Solis, and other officials examine a map showing the location of the [[Upper Big Branch Mine disaster]] in 2010]]

Solis became the first Hispanic woman to serve as a regular U.S. cabinet member and the first cabinet secretary with [[Central American]] descent.<ref name="naleo-pr">{{cite press release|url=http://www.naleo.org/pr/pr2-24-09NALEO.html |title=NALEO Congratulates Hilda L. Solis on Her Confirmation as Secretary of Labor |publisher=[[National Association of Latino Elected and Appointed Officials]] |date=February 24, 2009 |access-date=March 1, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100730234051/http://www.naleo.org/pr/pr2-24-09NALEO.html |archive-date=July 30, 2010}}</ref> She also became the first Hispanic Secretary of Labor.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.hispanicbusiness.com/politics/2009/2/24/hilda_solis_is_the_new_us.htm |title=Hilda Solis is the New U.S. Secretary of Labor |author=Kuznia, Rob |publisher=Hispanic Business |date=February 24, 2009 |access-date=March 1, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20130127054430/http://www.hispanicbusiness.com/politics/2009/2/24/hilda_solis_is_the_new_us.htm |archive-date=January 27, 2013 |df=mdy-all}}</ref> Solis felt that under the [[Presidency of George W. Bush|George W. Bush administration]], the department had become unimportant and lacking in power, and that its actions reflected a pro-business agenda.<ref name="nyt070509"/> Accordingly, she hoped to reinvigorate it.<ref name="nyt070509" />

[[File:Hilda Solis and Richard Chavez.jpg|thumb|right|Secretary Solis with farm worker organizer [[Richard Chavez]] in 2010, next to a mural depicting his brother [[César Chávez]] ]]

In her first days as secretary, Solis affirmed an extension to unemployment benefits specified by the [[American Recovery and Reinvestment Act of 2009|2009 Obama stimulus package]],<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.kansascity.com/business/story/1057373.html |title=New jobless claims hit 667,000 |author=Stafford, Diane |newspaper=[[Kansas City Star]] |date=February 26, 2009 |access-date=February 28, 2009 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090302145147/http://www.kansascity.com/business/story/1057373.html |archive-date=March 2, 2009}}</ref> and joined Vice President Biden's Middle Class Task Force.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.cnn.com/2009/POLITICS/02/27/middle.class.green/ |title=Green jobs in focus as task force on middle class begins work |publisher=[[CNN]] |date=February 27, 2009 |access-date=February 28, 2009}}</ref> In her first major speech as secretary, Solis pleased community forum attendees at [[Miami]]'s [[Greater Bethel AME Church (Miami, Florida)|Greater Bethel AME Church]] by vowing more aggressive enforcement of workplace protection laws, saying "You can rest assured that there is a new sheriff in town."<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2009/03/08/us/08labor.html |title=At Labor Gathering, Luxury, Jockeying and Applause for Secretary |author=Greenhouse, Steven |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=March 7, 2009 |access-date=March 8, 2009}}</ref>  In late March 2009, Solis vowed to add 250&nbsp;investigators to the department's Wage and Hour Division after a [[Government Accountability Office]] report showed the division's enforcement of wage laws was quite inadequate;<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB123801442734541143 |title=U.S. Steps Up Wage-Law Enforcement |author=Trottman, Melanie |newspaper=[[The Wall Street Journal]] |date=March 25, 2009 |access-date=March 27, 2009}}</ref> the staffing up was completed by the end of the year.<ref name="ap010110" /> In late May 2009, Solis suspended immigrant guest worker regulations related to [[H-2A visa]]s adopted in the final days of the Bush administration; the move earned plaudits from the [[United Farm Workers]].<ref>{{cite news |title=Rule Change for Workers on Farms |author=Preston, Julia |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=May 29, 2009}}</ref> In July 2009, she expressed concern about workplace deaths among Hispanics, which she said they were especially vulnerable to<ref>{{cite news |url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/printedition/news/20090720/1aworkerdeaths20_st.art.htm |title=Hispanic worker deaths up 76% |author=Jervis, Rick |newspaper=[[USA Today]] |date=July 20, 2009 |access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> (her continuing attention to issues such as this during her tenure would lead to Hispanic workers considering her their champion).<ref name="nyt-dol-resign" /> In October 2009, the [[Occupational Safety and Health Administration]] levied the largest fine in its history on [[BP]] for failing to fix safety problems following the 2005 [[Texas City Refinery disaster]].<ref name="ap010110">{{cite news |url=https://abcnews.go.com/Business/wireStory?id=9460816 |title=Labor Chief Moves on Job Safety, Workers' Rights |author=Hananel, Sam |agency=[[Associated Press]] |publisher=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |date=January 1, 2010 |access-date=January 9, 2010}}</ref> Business groups such as the [[National Federation of Independent Business]] complained that Solis was forging a less cooperative relationship, one that departed from the Bush administration's "compliance assistance" approach; the Labor Department said that compliance assistance was still an important part of the new strategy.<ref name="ap010110" />

[[File:G20 April 2010.jpg|thumb|left|upright|The April 2010 meeting of the [[G-20 major economies|G20 labor ministers]] at the Department of Labor was the first of its kind.]]

For 2010, Solis's agenda was to enact some ninety new rules and regulations intended to grant more power to unions and to workers.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB126020616287780209 |title=Solis Pushes Agenda to Bolster Labor |author=Trottman, Melanie |author2=Maher, Kris |newspaper=[[Wall Street Journal]] |date=December 8, 2009 |access-date=December 16, 2009}}</ref> Whether Solis would try to revive [[Clinton administration]] ergonomics rules that had been discarded in the early days of the Bush administration, and that business groups continued to oppose, was unclear.<ref name="ap010110" /> In the wake of the [[Upper Big Branch Mine disaster]] in [[West Virginia]] in April 2010, the worst in the U.S. in forty years, Solis announced that the Labor Department's [[Mine Safety and Health Administration]] would conduct an internal review of its enforcement of the [[Massey Energy]] mine prior to the accident.<ref name="cgm041610">{{cite news |url=http://sundaygazettemail.com/News/201004160784 |title=Probe to examine impact of surface blasting at Upper Big Branch |author=Ward, Ken Jr.|newspaper=[[Charleston Gazette-Mail]] |date=April 16, 2010 |access-date=April 16, 2010}}</ref>  She also requested that the [[National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health]] provide an independent analysis of that review.<ref name="cgm041610" /> (By the end of her tenure, however, some safety experts said she had fallen short of getting any meaningful new regulatory scheme in place in the wake of the disaster.<ref name="wapo-dol-resign" />) Later that month, Solis and the department hosted the first-ever meeting of the [[G-20 major economies|G-20 labor ministers]]; they discussed how to accelerate job creation in their respective countries.<ref>{{cite news |url=http://www.allheadlinenews.com/articles/7018471838 |title=G20 Ministers Agree On Acceleration Of Job Creation |author=Singh, Tejinder |agency=[[All Headline News]] |date=April 21, 2010 |access-date=April 26, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120119184327/http://www.allheadlinenews.com/articles/7018471838 |archive-date=January 19, 2012 |df=mdy-all}}</ref> Solis also faced disgruntlement from a local of the [[American Federation of Government Employees]] representing her own employees, who were unhappy that a longstanding [[flextime]] program reduced under the George W. Bush administration had not been restored.<ref name="wapo-local">{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/wp-dyn/content/article/2010/04/22/AR2010042205756.html |title=AFGE pushes for flextime at Labor Department |author=Kamen, Al |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=April 23, 2010 |access-date=April 26, 2010}}</ref> The department said the program was modern and fair and that it was part of ongoing contract negotiations with the local.<ref name="wapo-local"/> The year also saw the department trying to crack down on firms that illegally use summer internships for free labor, by clarifying what may constitute an unpaid academic internship;<ref>{{cite web|last=Wage and Hour Division|title=Fact Sheet #71: Internship Programs Under the Fair Labor Standards Act|url=http://www.dol.gov/whd/regs/compliance/whdfs71.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100602032839/http://www.dol.gov/whd/regs/compliance/whdfs71.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=June 2, 2010|publisher=[[U.S. Department of Labor]]|access-date=October 18, 2011}}</ref> the move brought resistance from universities.<ref>{{cite news|last=Lipka|first=Sara|title=Leave Internships to Us, College Leaders Tell Feds|url=http://chronicle.com/article/Leave-Internships-to-Us/65326/?sid=at|newspaper=[[The Chronicle of Higher Education]] |date=April 29, 2010}}</ref>  The year additionally saw Solis leading an administration campaign against farmers who employed children or underpaid workers.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/06/19/us/19migrant.html |title=U.S. Cracks Down on Farmers Who Hire Children |author=Eckholm, Erik |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=June 18, 2010 |access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> (Proposed new rules in this area were dropped in 2012, however, following adamant criticism from conservatives and agricultural groups.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.huffingtonpost.com/2012/04/27/white-house-child-labor-agriculture_n_1458701.html |title=Child Labor Farm Rules Scrapped By White House Under Political Pressure |author=Jamieson, Dave |work=[[HuffPost]] |date=April 27, 2012 |access-date=January 13, 2013}}</ref>)

[[File:General Motors Baltimore Operations Plant Tour with Solis and O'Malley.jpg|thumb|left|Secretary Solis touring a Maryland [[General Motors]] facility in 2012 with Governor [[Martin O'Malley]] ]]

In February 2011, as [[2011 Wisconsin protests|protests continued]] over [[Wisconsin]] Governor [[Scott Walker (politician)|Scott Walker]]'s proposal to limit that state's public employee unions' collective bargaining rights, and similar proposals were made in other states, Solis spoke out strongly and emotionally against such moves, saying "[those governors] aren't just asking workers to tighten their belts, they're demanding they give up their uniquely American rights as workers."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://whitehouse.blogs.cnn.com/2011/02/26/labor-secretary-solis-elections-do-matter/ |title=Labor Secretary Solis: 'Elections do matter' |author=Brusk, Steve |publisher=[[CNN]] |date=February 26, 2011 |access-date=March 1, 2011 |archive-date=March 1, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110301160339/http://whitehouse.blogs.cnn.com/2011/02/26/labor-secretary-solis-elections-do-matter/ |url-status=dead }}</ref> Overall, however, the Obama administration did not speak out forcefully against these moves.<ref name="lat-dol-resign"/>

In October 2012, Solis defended the work of the [[Bureau of Labor Statistics]], after the [[Current Population Survey]] it puts out monthly reported that [[unemployment in the United States]] had fallen below eight percent for this first time since Obama took office.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.politico.com/politico44/2012/10/solis-charges-of-cooking-numbers-ludicrous-137635.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121008002028/http://www.politico.com/politico44/2012/10/solis-charges-of-cooking-numbers-ludicrous-137635.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 8, 2012 |title=Solis: Charges of cooking numbers 'ludicrous' |author =Donovan Slack |newspaper=[[Politico]] |date=October 5, 2012}}</ref> Some critics, including former [[General Electric]] CEO [[Jack Welch]], charged that the number had been tampered with in order to benefit Obama one month before the [[2012 United States presidential election|U.S. presidential election]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://money.cnn.com/2012/10/05/news/economy/welch-unemployment-rate/index.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007035239/http://money.cnn.com/2012/10/05/news/economy/welch-unemployment-rate/index.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 7, 2012 |title=Jack Welch questions jobs numbers |author=Chris Isidore |publisher=[[CNNMoney]] |date=October 5, 2012}}</ref>  Solis said, "I'm insulted when I hear that because we have a very professional, civil service organization where you have top, top economists that work at the BLS. They've been doing these calculations. These are our best trained and best-skilled individuals working in the BLS, and it's really ludicrous to hear that kind of statement."<ref>{{cite news |url=http://latino.foxnews.com/latino/politics/2012/10/05/obama-labor-secretary-solis-insulted-by-claims-fixed-job-numbers/#ixzz28Tgwp6w1 |title=Obama Labor Secretary Solis 'Insulted' by Claims Job Numbers are Fixed |author=Llenas, Bryan |publisher=[[Fox News Latino]] |date=October 5, 2012 |access-date=October 5, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007232514/http://latino.foxnews.com/latino/politics/2012/10/05/obama-labor-secretary-solis-insulted-by-claims-fixed-job-numbers/#ixzz28Tgwp6w1 |archive-date=October 7, 2012 |url-status=dead |df=mdy-all}}</ref> For the year, the Labor Department set a record for the most back pay it had ever collected due to wage violations, $280&nbsp;million going to some 300,000&nbsp;workers.<ref name="nyt-dol-resign" /> Workplace fatalities in construction and general industrial sectors reached an all-time low.<ref name="lat-dol-resign" />

[[File:Hilda Solis last day DoL.jpg|thumb|right|On her last day as secretary, Solis was given a farewell gift of the chair she used in Cabinet meetings.]]

On January 9, 2013, Solis tendered her resignation as Secretary of Labor, becoming one of several Cabinet members deciding not to stay on for Obama's second term.<ref name="wapo-dol-resign">{{cite news |url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/business/economy/hilda-solis-resigns-as-labor-secretary/2013/01/09/1e9b9394-5aa3-11e2-9fa9-5fbdc9530eb9_story.html |title=Hilda Solis resigns as labor secretary; some others in Cabinet to stay on |author=Mufson, Steven |author2=Nakamura, David |newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] |date=January 9, 2013 |access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref> Her last day in office was January 22, 2013.<ref>{{cite news |last=Puga |first=Kristina |title=Secretary of Labor Hilda Solis bids farewell |url=http://nbclatino.com/2013/01/23/photos-secretary-of-labor-hilda-solis-bids-farewell/ |access-date=January 23, 2013 |publisher=[[NBCLatino]] |date=January 23, 2013 |archive-date=January 26, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130126013008/http://nbclatino.com/2013/01/23/photos-secretary-of-labor-hilda-solis-bids-farewell/ |url-status=dead}}</ref>

Solis, who had never become part of the inner circle of presidential advisors,<ref name="nyt-dol-resign" /> said it had been a difficult decision and Obama praised her work as secretary.<ref name="foxlat-dol-resign" /> Reflecting upon her tenure, Solis generally garnered praise from labor unions and leading Democrats for her stricter enforcement of job safety regulations and more aggressive pursuit of wage and hour violators.<ref name="nyt-dol-resign" /><ref name="wapo-dol-resign" /><ref name="foxlat-dol-resign" /> Other leaders and analysts in the labor field thought her performance as secretary was underwhelming, with minimal public visibility and no memorable legacy left behind.<ref name="lat-dol-resign">{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/news/nationworld/nation/la-na-solis-labor-20130110,0,7622972.story |title=Labor Secretary Solis says she's returning to California |author=Semuels, Alana |author2=Reston, Maeve |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=January 9, 2013 |access-date=January 13, 2013}}</ref> All agreed that she operated in a difficult political environment, with the effects of the [[Great Recession]] still being felt, Republicans staunchly opposed to labor-based initiatives, and the Obama administration's attentions focused elsewhere.<ref name="wapo-dol-resign" /><ref name="lat-dol-resign" /> Business groups, meanwhile, continued to characterize her as having been uncooperative in her dealings with them.<ref name="nyt-dol-resign">{{cite news |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2013/01/10/business/solis-stepping-down-as-labor-secretary.html?_r=0 |title=Solis Stepping Down as Labor Secretary |author=Landler, Mark |author2=Greenhouse, Steven |newspaper=[[The New York Times]] |date=January 9, 2013 |access-date=January 9, 2013}}</ref><ref name="foxlat-dol-resign" />

During early 2014, reports emerged that the [[United States Office of Special Counsel]], the [[United States Department of Justice]], and the [[FBI]] had begun investigating Solis during 2012 for possible violations of fundraising rules by federal officials during her time as Labor Secretary. Allegations were made that Solis solicited subordinates for funds for the [[Barack Obama presidential campaign, 2012|2012 re-election campaign of President Obama]]. A spokesperson for Solis said that she believed she had done nothing wrong.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/local/la-me-solis-investigation-20140510-story.html |title=Complaint over Obama fundraiser triggered Solis probe |author=Pringle, Paul |author2=Sewell, Abby |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=May 9, 2014 |access-date=June 5, 2014}}</ref> The matter was also being looked into by the [[House Oversight and Government Reform Committee]] and its chair, Representative [[Darrell Issa]], who said there was evidence supporting the allegations.<ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-hilda-solis-recording-20140716-story.html |title=Rep. Issa says recording is evidence of improper fundraising by Solis |author=Sewell, Abby |newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] |date=July 16, 2014 |access-date=July 27, 2014}}</ref> By early 2016, no further word had emerged on any of these investigations.

==Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors==
Solis's departure from the Labor Department was speculated as a preparation for a run for a seat on the [[Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors]] in 2014, to replace the term-limited incumbent, [[Los Angeles County Supervisorial Districts|1st District]] supervisor [[Gloria Molina]].<ref name="foxlat-dol-resign">{{cite news | url=http://latino.foxnews.com/latino/politics/2013/01/09/hilda-solis-resigns-as-labor-secretary/ | title=Hilda Solis Resigns as Labor Secretary | author=Llorente, Elizabeth | publisher=[[Fox News Latino]] | date=January 9, 2013 | access-date=January 9, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130113032301/http://latino.foxnews.com/latino/politics/2013/01/09/hilda-solis-resigns-as-labor-secretary/ | archive-date=January 13, 2013 | url-status=dead | df=mdy-all }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | url=http://blogs.laweekly.com/informer/2013/01/hilda_solis_resigns_secretary_of_labor_los_angeles_supervisors_county_federation_of_labor_maria_elena_durazo.php | title=Hilda Solis Resigns As Obama's Secretary Of Labor, Could Be Returning To L.A. Politics | author=Romero, Dennis | newspaper=[[LA Weekly]] | date=January 9, 2013 | access-date=January 9, 2013 | archive-date=January 16, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130116032947/http://blogs.laweekly.com/informer/2013/01/hilda_solis_resigns_secretary_of_labor_los_angeles_supervisors_county_federation_of_labor_maria_elena_durazo.php | url-status=dead }}</ref>  Officially, Solis only said that she wanted to rest, reconnect with her local community after twelve years in Washington, and spend time with her mother, who was 87 years old at the time.<ref name="lat-considering"/>

Later during January 2013, Solis confirmed her interest in [[2014 Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors election|the County Board of Supervisors race]], saying "I'm going to take a look at it."<ref name="lat-considering">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/la-xpm-2013-jan-18-la-pn-hilda-solis-county-board-of-supervisors-20130118-story.html | title=Hilda Solis considering a run for L.A.
