County Board of Supervisors | author=Simon, Richard | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=January 18, 2013 | access-date=April 11, 2013}}</ref>  In explaining why a former U.S. Representative and Cabinet member would be interested in a county-level body, analysts stated that the board is the most powerful county-level legislative body in the United States,<ref name="fox-lat-power"/> and exercises some executive and quasi-judicial powers as well.<ref name="fnl-sup-elec"/>  It controls a workforce larger than the Labor Department's<ref name="lat-considering"/> and its $26 billion budget is equivalent to that of an average U.S. state.<ref name="wapo-sup-elec"/> Each member presiding over some two million constituents, three times that of Solis' old congressional district,<ref name="wapo-sup-elec"/> and that it is quite possibly the fourth most powerful position in California politics, after governor, U.S. Senator, and mayor of Los Angeles.<ref name="lat-considering"/><ref name="fox-lat-power">{{cite news | url=http://latino.foxnews.com/latino/politics/2013/01/10/hilda-solis-may-be-eyeing-run-for-powerful-la-county-board-supervisor-position/ | title=Hilda Solis Set to Become Queen of LA After Resignation, Eyes Powerful County Position | author=Llenas, Bryan | publisher=[[Fox News Latino]] | date=January 10, 2013 | access-date=April 12, 2013 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130310054530/http://latino.foxnews.com/latino/politics/2013/01/10/hilda-solis-may-be-eyeing-run-for-powerful-la-county-board-supervisor-position/ | archive-date=March 10, 2013 | url-status=dead | df=mdy-all }}</ref>  The supervisors have long been nicknamed "the five little kings".<ref name="wapo-sup-elec"/>

In November 2013, Solis became a scholar-in-residence at her ''alma mater'' of [[Cal Poly Pomona]].  Her duties were to include  guest lecturing in classes, mentoring students, and assisting in curriculum development, with a focus in political science.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://touch.latimes.com/#section/-1/article/p2p-78283409/ | title=Former Labor Secretary Hilda Solis takes Cal Poly Pomona post | author=Rivera, Carla | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=November 21, 2013 | access-date=November 24, 2013 | archive-date=October 6, 2012 | archive-url=http://webarchive.loc.gov/all/20121006015957/http://touch.latimes.com/#section/-1/article/p2p-78283409/ | url-status=dead }}</ref>

[[Image:Mayor Eric Garcetti and County Supervisor Hilda Solis (15472578322).jpg|thumb|right|Newly elected Supervisor Solis with Mayor of Los Angeles [[Eric Garcetti]] in 2014]]

On April 5, 2014, Solis formally announced the start of her campaign for the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors seat, with the election to be held on June 3.<ref name="lat-kickoff">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-solis-county-campaign-20140405,0,6458272.story#axzz2yTfbNmLy | title=Hilda Solis officially kicks off campaign for county supervisor | first=Abby | last=Sewell | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=April 5, 2014 | access-date=April 10, 2014}}</ref>  By this time she had raised over $600,000 for her effort and was considered the favorite to win the contest.<ref name="lat-kickoff"/>  News of the federal investigation had little effect on her campaign.<ref name="fnl-sup-elec"/>  Solis won the seat on June 4, 2014,<ref name="fnl-sup-elec">{{cite news | url=http://latino.foxnews.com/latino/politics/2014/06/04/hilda-solis-former-labor-chief-wins-seat-on-la-county-board-supervisors/ | title=Hilda Solis, Former Labor Chief, Wins Seat On Powerful L.A. County Board of Supervisors | publisher=[[Fox News Latino]] | date=June 4, 2014 | access-date=June 4, 2014 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140607001926/http://latino.foxnews.com/latino/politics/2014/06/04/hilda-solis-former-labor-chief-wins-seat-on-la-county-board-supervisors/ | archive-date=June 7, 2014 | url-status=dead | df=mdy-all }}</ref> garnering 70&nbsp;percent of the vote against two other opponents.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://rrccmain.co.la.ca.us/14062043/2043_c2897.htm | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140606233152/http://rrccmain.co.la.ca.us/14062043/2043_c2897.htm | url-status=dead | archive-date=June 6, 2014 | title=Supervisor – 1st District | publisher=[[Los Angeles County, California|Los Angeles County]] | access-date=June 4, 2014 }}</ref>  The margin meant she won the seat outright and would not need to run in a runoff election.<ref name="wapo-sup-elec">{{cite news | url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/blogs/govbeat/wp/2014/06/04/from-white-house-cabinet-to-county-office-why-hilda-solis-is-back-home/ | title=From White House cabinet to county office: Why Hilda Solis is back home | author=Chokshi, Niraj | newspaper=[[The Washington Post]] | date=June 4, 2014 | access-date=June 4, 2014}}</ref>

As Supervisor for District 1, she was at the forefront of the response to the [[Exide lead contamination]] issue, which affected [[Vernon, California|Vernon]] and several other communities within her purview and which touched upon her past concerns with environmental justice.<ref name="ladn-exide"/>  The Supervisors allocated some county money for cleanup, with Solis saying, "the state continues to drag its feet".<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-la-exide-cleanup-county-supervisors-20151027-story.html|title=Exide cleanup: L.A. County approves $2 million to speed lead removal at homes|first=Tony |last=Barboza|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date= October 27, 2015|access-date=February 7, 2016}}</ref> Going to the state capitol and asking for additional funds to remedy the situation, she said, "This has gone on too long."<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.latimes.com/politics/la-pol-sac-exide-cleanup-legislators-20160126-story.html|title=L.A.-area and state officials call for quicker cleanup of Exide plant contamination|first=Melanie |last=Mason|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date= January 26, 2016|access-date=February 25, 2016}}</ref> In February 2016 she praised Governor [[Jerry Brown]] for finally increasing state funds for the cleanup, saying "Our voices were heard. For too long we have seen two Americas: one in which affluent neighborhoods get immediate help and relief. The other America is made up of poor working-class families who silently suffer. Today's announcement from the governor reconciles these two Americas."<ref name="ladn-exide">{{cite news | url=http://www.dailynews.com/environment-and-nature/20160217/supervisor-hilda-solis-on-exide-clean-up-funds-two-americas-for-too-long | title=Supervisor Hilda Solis on Exide clean-up funds: 'Two Americas' for too long | first=Sarah | last=Favot | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] | date=February 17, 2016 | access-date=February 28, 2016}}</ref>

Among the other areas Solis was responsible for was [[Downtown Los Angeles]].<ref name="ladt-prio"/> There she said her main priority was dealing with [[gentrification]] and the lack of [[affordable housing]].<ref name="ladt-prio">{{cite news | url=http://www.ladowntownnews.com/news/a-q-a-with-downtown-county-supervisor-hilda-solis/article_6e53af84-d184-11e4-8a94-9716d0a5a176.html | title=A Q&A With Downtown County Supervisor Hilda Solis | first=Eddie | last=Kim | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Downtown News]] | date=March 24, 2015 | access-date=February 28, 2016}}</ref> By 2017, data showed that, under her tenure, the homeless rate had gone up by 48 percent in her district,<ref name="latimeslacountyhomelessnessjumps">{{cite news|last1=Holland|first1=Gale|last2=Smith|first2=Doug|title=L.A. County homelessness jumps a 'staggering' 23% as need far outpaces housing, new count shows|url=https://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-homeless-count-20170530-story.html|access-date=May 31, 2017|newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=May 31, 2017|quote=In the big picture of Los Angeles County, the most drastic increase — 48% — occurred in the San Gabriel Valley district of Supervisor Hilda Solis, where the count rose to just under 13,000.}}</ref> with a 36 percent increase in the San Gabriel Valley itself.<ref name="psn-homeless"/>  The increase was attributed by officials familiar with the problem to constantly increasing housing costs combined with flat incomes.<ref name="latimeslacountyhomelessnessjumps"/>  Solis said in response, "With increasingly out-of-control rents, we need more tools to secure housing stability for the most vulnerable County residents."<ref name="psn-homeless">{{cite news | url=https://www.pasadenastarnews.com/2017/05/31/san-gabriel-valley-homeless-count-up-36-percent-volunteers-found-a-big-jump-in-homeless-veterans/ | title=San Gabriel Valley homeless count up 36 percent, volunteers found a big jump in homeless veterans | first=Christopher | last=Yee | newspaper=[[Pasadena Star-News]] | date=May 31, 2017 | access-date=June 3, 2017}}</ref>

[[Image:Hilda Solis at Ricardo F Icaza Workers Center Grand Opening 2017.jpg|thumb|left|Supervisor Solis at a local union office opening in 2017]]

Regarding the new job as a whole, Solis said, "It's fascinating how many people work for the county – over 100,000. At the Department of Labor it was like 15,000. The budget here is $26 billion, much more than what I was used to in D.C."<ref name="ladt-prio"/>  In December 2015 Solis took over as [[Los Angeles County Chair|Chair of the Supervisors]], a position which is rotated on a yearly basis.<ref name="ladn-chair">{{cite news | url=http://www.dailynews.com/government-and-politics/20151208/hilda-solis-will-chair-la-county-board-of-supervisors-for-the-next-year | title=Hilda Solis will chair LA County Board of Supervisors for the next year | agency=[[City News Service]] | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] | date=December 8, 2015 | access-date=February 28, 2016}}</ref> She said a priority for 2016 would be "to reaffirm our commitment to our diverse county family – to make this family, our family, inclusive for everybody, no matter their background, no matter where they come from, no matter how far down the scale they have been."<ref name="ladn-chair"/>  One of her efforts went towards getting additional resources for older children who were transitioning out of the [[foster care]] system.<ref name="lat-unopp"/>

Following the results of the [[2016 United States presidential election]] and the fear of mass deportations that ensued due to the victor, Solis worked together with Los Angeles Mayor [[Eric Garcetti]] to create the $10 million  L.A. Justice Fund, which would provide legal services to illegal immigrants facing deportation.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://ktla.com/2017/04/17/l-a-legal-fund-aims-to-help-immigrants-facing-deportation-draws-criticism-over-who-deserves-representation/ | title=L.A. Legal Fund Aims to Help Immigrants Facing Deportation, Draws Criticism Over Who Deserves Representation | agency=[[Los Angeles Times]] | publisher=[[KTLA]] | date=April 17, 2017 | access-date=June 9, 2018}}</ref>

In May 2017, Solis voted in favor of retaining designation of the [[San Gabriel Mountains National Monument]], created in 2014 but under review, along with other recently created national monuments, by new U.S. Secretary of the Interior [[Ryan Zinke]] for possible revocation.<ref>{{cite news | url=http://www.sgvtribune.com/government-and-politics/20170502/la-county-supports-keeping-san-gabriel-mountains-as-national-monument | title=LA County supports keeping San Gabriel Mountains as national monument | first=Elizabeth | last=Marcellino | agency=[[City News Service]] | newspaper=[[San Gabriel Valley Tribune]] | date=May 2, 2017 | access-date=June 3, 2017}}</ref>  Solis also favored a [[parcel tax]] to increase the number of parks and playgrounds in Los Angeles.<ref name="lat-unopp"/>  In October 2017 a motion that she authored passed the board and resulted in [[Columbus Day]] being replaced as an official holiday in Los Angeles County by [[Indigenous Peoples' Day (United States)|Indigenous Peoples Day]].  She said in a statement, "This action is about publicly recognizing that America's ancestors, for centuries, oppressed certain minority groups. This is not about erasing history; I believe the full history and impact of Christopher Columbus should be taught to current and future generations. While we cannot change the past, we can realize the pain that millions suffered throughout our nation's history, as well as the tremendous achievements of the original inhabitants of our continent."<ref>{{cite news | url=https://abcnews.go.com/US/history-columbus-day-indigenous-peoples-day/story?id=50330413 | title=The history behind Columbus Day and Indigenous Peoples Day | publisher=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] | date=October 9, 2017 | access-date=October 21, 2017 }} See also [http://hildalsolis.org/supervisor-solis-motion-ends-columbus-day-county-holiday-replaces-it-with-indigenous-peoples-day/ "Supervisor Solis' Motion Ends 'Columbus Day' County Holiday, Replaces It With 'Indigenous Peoples Day"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171022085653/http://hildalsolis.org/supervisor-solis-motion-ends-columbus-day-county-holiday-replaces-it-with-indigenous-peoples-day/ |date=2017-10-22 }} from Solis's website.</ref>

[[Image:L.A. County Supervisor Hilda L. Solis attends Families Belong Together March 02.jpg|thumb|right|Supervisor Solis speaking at a 2018 [[Families Belong Together]] rally in protest of the White House's [[family separation in U.S. border enforcement]] ]]

In January 2018, Solis and the other supervisors supported the appointment of Nicole Tinkham as interim public defender, despite a letter signed by 390 public defenders who were concerned that Tinkham lacked criminal law experience and the potential for a conflict of interest, given Tinkham's prior representation of the [[Los Angeles County Sheriff's Department]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://theavtimes.com/2018/01/23/hundreds-of-deputy-public-defenders-protest-choice-of-new-interim-leader/|title=Hundreds of deputy public defenders protest choice of new interim leader|agency=[[City News Service]]|newspaper=The Antelope Valley Times|language=en-US|date=January 23, 2018|access-date=February 10, 2018}}</ref>

In the [[2018 Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors election]], Solis ran unopposed, and was accordingly re-elected on June 5, 2018.   A lack of serious opposition, or any opposition at all, is not unusual for incumbent Supervisors.<ref name="lat-unopp">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/local/lanow/la-me-ln-solis-kuehl-election-20180601-story.html | title=L.A. County supervisors rarely lose a reelection bid. That probably won't change on Tuesday | first=Nina | last=Agrawal | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=June 2, 2018 | access-date=June 8, 2018}}</ref>

In 2019, Solis, with fellow supervisor [[Sheila Kuehl]], was a leader of the successful effort to stop a planned $1.7&nbsp;billion mental health treatment center in the downtown area, intended to replace [[Men's Central Jail]].  Solis and others argued that the new facility would become a de facto jail and instead urged the creation of smaller treatment facilities spread around the county.  Solis said in reference to contractors for any such project, "I don't want to see people who are just used to building brick and mortar. I want to see people who have a humanistic approach."<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.dailynews.com/2019/08/13/la-county-supervisors-scrap-1-7-bill-contract-to-replace-jail-its-time-to-do-the-right-thing/ | title=LA County supervisors scrap $1.7 billion contract to replace jail: 'It's time to do the right thing' | first=Elizabeth | last=Marcellino | agency=[[City News Service]] | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] | date=August 13, 2019 | access-date=August 17, 2019}}</ref>
During the year, Solis also became an active supporter for [[Joe Biden 2020 presidential campaign|Joe Biden's 2020 presidential campaign]], saying that the former vice president, whom she dealt with during her time as Secretary of Labor, had the necessary "steady hand and experience" and who also is "personable" and can interact well with a wide range of people.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/news/politics-and-government/hilda-solis-a-biden-surrogate-says-hes-warm-experienced-1837439/ | title=Hilda Solis, a Biden surrogate, says he's warm, experienced | first=Rory | last=Appleton | newspaper=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] | date=August 29, 2019 | access-date=September 2, 2019}}</ref>

[[Image:Los Angeles County Supervisor Hilda Solis gives testimony to Subcommittee on Water Resources and Environment.jpg|thumb|left|Supervisor Solis testifying at an environmental hearing in early March 2020]]

The year 2020 was marked by the [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States]], and Solis and the other supervisors consistently urged residents to [[Social distancing measures related to the COVID-19 pandemic|stay at home and use other social distancing measures]].<ref name="lat-covid"/>  However some county employees in the districts of Solis and another supervisor complained that they were being compelled to report to unsafe offices instead of being allowed to work remotely.<ref name="lat-covid"/>  Solis said that the services provided by some positions could only be done in person, but following newspaper inquiries on the matter, remote work was opened up to more county workers.<ref name="lat-covid">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2020-07-22/county-supervisors-required-employees-to-report-to-the-office-open-staff-letter-alleges | title=Two L.A. County supervisors tout pandemic safety, but put own employees at risk, staffers say | author-first=Jaclyn | author-last=Cosgrove | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=July 22, 2020 | access-date=December 29, 2020}}</ref>  In December 2020, Solis became [[Los Angeles County Chair|rotating chair of the board]] again, and by then the entire board was women, a first for the county and something that Solis said was a historic accomplishment.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.dailynews.com/2020/12/08/l-a-county-supervisor-hilda-solis-takes-the-gavel-for-new-all-woman-board/ | title=L.A. County Supervisor Hilda Solis takes the gavel for new, all-woman board | author-first=David | author-last=Rosenfeld | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Daily News]] | date=December 8, 2020 | access-date=December 29, 2020}}</ref>  As the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Los Angeles|pandemic in Los Angeles]] reached an especially high peak towards the end of the year, Solis pleaded with county residents to stay home: "As we near Christmas, I urge everyone to cancel their holiday plans to gather with members outside of one's households. This will save many lives."<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.nbclosangeles.com/news/local/la-county-official-pleads-with-residents-stay-home/2490684/ | title=LA County Official Pleads With Residents: 'Stay Home' | agency=[[City News Service]] | publisher=[[KNBC]] | date=December 21, 2020 | access-date=December 29, 2020}}</ref>

The pandemic subsequently ebbed for a while, but then by mid-2021 the highly infectious [[SARS-CoV-2 Delta variant|Delta variant]] had become a significant threat, and in July 2021 Solis issued an executive order reimposing an indoors mask mandate within the county.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.msn.com/en-us/news/us/reinstating-mask-mandate-in-la-not-punishment-but-prevention-solis/ar-AAMhV5O | title=New mask mandate 'not punishment, but prevention': County official | agency=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] | publisher=[[MSN]] | date=July 18, 2021 | access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref>  By this point [[COVID-19 vaccination in the United States]] was well underway but also increasingly the subject of political disputes.  Saying that "As vaccinations continue at a pace slower than what is necessary to slow the spread, the need for immediate action is great," Solis issued a mandate in August 2021 that county employees, who numbered over a hundred thousand, be vaccinated by October 1.<ref name="lat-vax-mandate">{{cite news | url=https://www.latimes.com/california/story/2021-08-04/la-county-executive-order-mandates-employees-get-vaccinated | title=Solis issues executive order mandating L.A. County employees get vaccinated | author-first=Kevin | author-last=Rector | newspaper=[[Los Angeles Times]] | date=August 4, 2021 | access-date=October 19, 2021}}</ref>  Her action gave no option for regular testing and thus went further than most such mandates elsewhere in California and the rest of the country.<ref name="
lat-vax-mandate"/>

In 2024 and 2025, Solis and Supervisor [[Lindsey Horvath]] co-authored motions to adopt default [[plant-based diet|plant-based]] food procurement and expand plant-based food options at county events and institutions. The motions sought to reduce the county's food-related [[greenhouse gas emissions]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Mridul |first1=Anay |title=Los Angeles County Passes Law to Make All Departmental Food Purchases Plant-Based |url=https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/los-angeles-county-plant-based-department-horvath-solis/ |access-date=1 August 2025 |work=Green Queen |date=29 February 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240305225910/https://www.greenqueen.com.hk/los-angeles-county-plant-based-department-horvath-solis/ |archive-date=5 March 2024 |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |last1=Stone |first1=Erin |title=Moving to plant-based foods: LA County expanding program to cut down on emissions |url=https://laist.com/news/climate-environment/plant-based-foods-la-county-expanding-program-emissions |access-date=1 August 2025 |work=LAist |date=7 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250109160301/https://laist.com/news/climate-environment/plant-based-foods-la-county-expanding-program-emissions |archive-date=9 January 2025 |url-status=live }}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
[[File:Ms. magazine Cover - Fall 2011.jpg|thumb|Ms. magazine cover (2011)]]
As mentioned, in 2000, Solis was given the [[Profile in Courage Award]] by the [[John F. Kennedy Library Foundation]].<ref name="jfk052200"/>

In 2010, Solis received the inaugural Robert P. Biller Award for Exemplary Public Service from the University of Southern California's [[School of Policy, Planning, and Development]].<ref>{{cite news | url=https://news.usc.edu/26887/SPPD-Alumna-Hilda-Solis-Receives-Biller-Award/ | title=SPPD Alumna Hilda Solis Receives Biller Award | author-first=Jan | author-last=Peterson | work=USC News | publisher=University of Southern California | date=November 19, 2010 | accessdate=May 9, 2023 | archive-date=June 15, 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230615214517/https://news.usc.edu/26887/SPPD-Alumna-Hilda-Solis-Receives-Biller-Award/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> The Hispanic Association of Colleges & Universities named Solis as the recipient of its 2011 President's Award for Excellence.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://www.hacu.net/NewsBot.asp?MODE=VIEW&ID=1129 | title=HACU presents award to Secretary of Labor | publisher=Hispanic Association of Colleges & Universities  | date=May 3, 2012 | access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> In  2012, Solis received the Champion for the Futures of Farmworker Children Award from the  Association of Farmworker Opportunity Programs.<ref>{{cite press release | url=https://www.dol.gov/newsroom/releases/opa/opa20120531 | title=Secretary of Labor Hilda L. Solis receives award from Association of Farmworker Opportunity Programs | publisher=U.S. Department of Labor | date=May 31, 2012 | access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> That same year, Solis was given a President's Award from an organization associated with [[California State University, Los Angeles]].<ref>{{cite press release | url=https://www.calstatela.edu/univ/ppa/newsrel/ecst-gala2012.htm | title=Cal State L.A. honors U.S. Secretary of Labor Hilda Solis with the 'President's Award' during 3rd annual Greater Los Angeles Engineer of the Year Gala | publisher=California State University, Los Angeles | date=July 30, 2012 | access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> The [[Imagen Foundation]] honored Solis with its President's Award in 2016, with the presentation being done by the actress [[America Ferrera]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.imagen.org/2016/07/hon-hilda-l-solis-imagen-presidents-award-recipient/ | title=Hon. Hilda L. Solis, Imagen President's Award Recipient | publisher=The Imagen Foundation | date=July 17, 2016| access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> In 2019, Solis received the Leadership Award at the annual American Latino Influencer Awards.<ref>{{cite press release | url=https://americanlatinomuseum.org/la-county-supervisor-hilda-l-solis-to-receive-leadership-award-at-2019-american-latino-influencer-awards/
 | title=LA County Supervisor Hilda L. Solis to Receive Leadership Award at 2019 American Latino Influencer Awards | publisher=Friends of the American Latino Museum | access-date=May 3, 2023}}</ref>

Solis gave the commencement address at [[Rio Hondo College]] in 2014, where she had once been on the board of trustees.<ref>{{cite press release | url=https://caschoolnews.net/articles/hilda-solis-to-offer-commencement-address-at-rio-hondo-college/ | title=Hilda Solis Offered Commencement Address at Rio Hondo College | work=California School News Report | date=May 27, 2014 | access-date=May 8, 2023 | archive-date=May 8, 2023 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230508103707/https://caschoolnews.net/articles/hilda-solis-to-offer-commencement-address-at-rio-hondo-college/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> In recognition of her long career in public service, she was in 2023 awarded an honorary doctor of laws degree by the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]].<ref name="unc-2023">{{cite web | url=https://www.unc.edu/posts/2023/03/27/honorary-degrees-go-to-six-leaders-in-policy-justice-and-fashion/ | date=March 27, 2023 | work=The Well newsletter | publisher=University of North Carolina | title=Honorary degrees go to six leaders in policy, justice and fashion}}</ref>

Several entities have been named after Solis. Beginning in the 1990s, the Hilda L. Solis Scholarship Dinner & Reception has been given annually by her alma mater, California State Polytechnic University, Pomona, with a large number of students having benefitted from receiving scholarships.<ref>{{cite news | url=https://polycentric.cpp.edu/2018/09/hilda-solis-scholarship-honors-difference-makers/ | title=Hilda Solis Scholarship Honors Difference Makers | publisher=University News Center | date= September 19, 2018 | access-date=May 9, 2023}} <!-- see also e.g. https://thepolypost.com/news/2012/05/29/article_043b1cfc-a957-11e1-b9fa-0019bb30f31a-8/ --></ref>
The Hilda L. Solis Care First Village is a set of housing units intended for the homeless that are put together using [[modular building]] techniques and located in Downtown Los Angeles.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.modular.org/awards-the-hilda-l-solis-care-first-village/ | title=The Hilda L. Solis Care First Village | publisher=Modular Building Institute | access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref> The Hilda L. Solis Learning Academy School of Technology, Business and Education is located in the general [[East Los Angeles]] area and  is part of the [[Los Angeles Unified School District]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.cde.ca.gov/schooldirectory/details?cdscode=19647330126474 | title=California School Directory: Hilda L. Solis Learning Academy School of Technology, Business and Education | publisher=California Department of Education | access-date=May 9, 2023 <!-- see also https://www.greatschools.org/california/los-angeles/27006-Hilda-L.-Solis-Learning-Academy-School-Of-Technology-Business-And-Education/
 -->}}</ref>

In 2022, the White House appointed Solis to [[John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts#Board of trustees|the Board of Trustees]] for the [[John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts]].<ref>{{cite press release | url=https://bidenwhitehouse.archives.gov/briefing-room/statements-releases/2022/10/26/president-biden-announces-key-appointments-to-the-board-of-trustees-of-the-john-f-kennedy-center-for-the-performing-arts/ | title=President Biden Announces Key Appointments to the Board of Trustees of the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts | publisher=The White House | date=October 26, 2022 | access-date=May 9, 2023}}</ref>
